title: Every Building Is a Balance Sheet: Spatial Memory for Real-World Assets — Jordi Spranger, Spranic
talk_summary: A pitch for Spranic's spatial-memory product: walk a building with an off-the-shelf sensor, get a semantic graph of objects, re-walk later and diff the two captures to detect changes, then query it in natural language. It is a real-estate/insurance vertical demo, not an agent-engineering talk.

takeaways.what_they_do: Each capture of the same space is aligned to prior captures on a time axis, and queries ask 'what changed' object-by-object rather than 'what is there', with each delta linked back to the source capture as evidence.
takeaways.evidence_quote: two walks of one space compare object by object and and surrounding by surrounding. You also want to know when it has changed.

takeaways.technique: Graph-backed semantic index over raw captures
takeaways.what_they_do: Raw sensor captures are converted into a semantic graph so that questions are answered by traversal ('where can I heat myself' -> radiator) rather than by feeding pixels to a model.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it makes the map from pixels into something we can work with.
